clinician.final_diagnosis: K. pneumoniae EE with wide retinal necrosis in a previously healthy subject
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 72-year-old immunocompetent male presented with severe high fever and gastrointestinal and genitourinary symptoms, diagnosed with acute prostatitis. Urine culture confirmed ampicillin-resistant K. pneumoniae. Three days after admission, he developed floaters and vision loss in his right eye. Ophthalmological examination revealed severe intraocular inflammation, including marked anterior chamber exudation, opaque fundus view, and vitreous hyper-reflective signal compatible with abscess or hemorrhage. Initial topical treatment was ineffective. He subsequently underwent urgent pars plana vitrectomy and vitreous biopsy, along with intravitreal antibiotics. Intraoperatively, the retina showed moderate ischemia, vasculitis, and an infiltrated area.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with acute prostatitis caused by ampicillin-resistant K. pneumoniae.
Three days after admission, patient developed floaters and vision loss in the right eye.

Ophthalmological examination revealed severe right eye inflammation and vitreous findings consistent with infection (BCVA hand motion, marked anterior chamber exudation, opaque fundus view, vitreous hyper-reflective signal compatible with abscess or hemorrhage).
Patient underwent urgent pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) and vitreous biopsy with intravitreal antibiotics.
Intraoperative findings during PPV included moderately ischemic retina, signs of vasculitis, and an area of infiltrated retina.

remaining_uncertainties: Direct microbiological confirmation of K. pneumoniae from the vitreous biopsy specimen.
Explicit confirmation of 'wide retinal necrosis' as described in the final diagnosis, beyond the observed ischemic and infiltrated retina.
Specific treatment response or outcome of the endophthalmitis after PPV and intravitreal antibiotics.
